articles.title: 9 ways to save money and avoid debt this Black Friday
articles.summary: Having a plan ready can help you avoid debt during Black Friday shopping — especially if you're using a credit card.
articles.body:
Some offers on this page are from advertisers who pay us, which may affect which products we write about, but not our recommendations. See our Advertiser Disclosure .

As retailers roll out early deals throughout November, Black Friday can seem more like an entire season than a single shopping day. But despite the early discounts, many Americans are still waiting until Thanksgiving weekend to tackle their holiday shopping.

Nearly two-thirds (64%) of consumers say they're likely to wait until Thanksgiving weekend to do most of their holiday shopping, according to a 2026 National Retail Federation survey . But affordability is also top of mind: 56% of holiday shoppers say the state of the economy will affect their spending plans this year.

Completing your holiday shopping list doesn't have to leave your bank account empty come January, though. Have a financial plan ready to help you avoid overspending this year — especially if you're using a credit card.

Here are a few things to keep in mind to avoid debt and save money this Black Friday and beyond.

Decide on a budget to guide your spending before you head out this Black Friday. Maybe it's the total you've already set aside in savings throughout the year for holiday shopping or simply a portion of your normal budget.

You can also get specific by breaking up your overall budget into subcategories. Say you have $500 to spend on Black Friday deals. If your main goal is to cross off the majority of your gift list, maybe you'll allocate $400 of that to gifts while reserving $100 for any great savings you come across for yourself.

Take a look back at last year's spending to help you budget better this year, too. Review your old statements and receipts. Were you satisfied with the amount you spent, or are there items you wouldn't repurchase?

Online and in-store retailers alike may bombard you with limited-time offers and must-have new items, but making a game plan before you shop can help you avoid falling prey.

Many big-box retailers and plenty of smaller merchants release Black Friday or Cyber Monday deals in the weeks leading up to the big shopping days. Use these previews to find savings on the items you need and make your shopping list early. And don't forget to look for roundups online cataloging the year's best discounts.

Once you have your list, compare prices across a few retailers. Just because an item is on sale doesn't mean you're getting the lowest available price.

If you're unsure whether you'll be able to pay down your balance in full by the time your monthly payment is due, a card with a 0% APR introductory offer for new purchases could be worth considering. After you open your account, you'll have several months (typically between 12 and 18) to pay down your balance before interest kicks in.

Just remember: You'll still need to make at least your minimum payment each month and pay your purchases off in full by the time the intro period ends. Otherwise, you'll start to accrue interest on your remaining balance at the standard APR, just like any other credit card.

Here are a few top 0% APR offers available today:

4. Rethink nonessentials if you already have credit card debt

Most shoppers' email inboxes are flooded even more than usual with deals and discounts throughout the holiday shopping season. But for some people, this might be a time to reduce spending instead of splurging.

If you already have credit card debt, consider whether Black Friday shopping is a good idea this year. Instead, reward yourself by making an extra payment toward your balances.

Consider using a cash-only method for holiday shopping. Withdraw only the amount of cash you can spend on gifts and other purchases, and leave your credit cards at home. And if you haven't already developed a debt payoff plan, start getting ahead of the issue now.

5. Take advantage of credit card rewards

Credit card rewards can offer a big boost to your holiday shopping savings. Take a look at the rewards categories on the cards already in your wallet before you start shopping. If you're doing most of your Black Friday shopping online, for example, you may have a card that earns bonus cash back on online retail purchases. Or if you're shopping at several different types of retailers, a card with a flat rewards rate on all purchases could make more sense.

Say you spend $500 on holiday gifts using a credit card that earns 2% cash back on all purchases. That's $10 in cash back on purchases you were already planning to make.

Just make sure you can pay off your balance in full by your payment due date. The interest you could accrue by carrying a balance can quickly outweigh the value of any rewards you earn.

Before you shop, look beyond sale prices for other opportunities to score deals. If you're shopping online, consider using browser extensions that can scour the internet for coupons and cash-back offers you may qualify for. In-store, some Black Friday retailers may price match discounts from other stores, helping you save the difference at checkout. Check the retailer's policy first, since some exclude Black Friday deals from price matching.

Start watching prices early and set up price alert notifications for items you want. Knowing what regular prices are in the weeks leading up to a big sale can help you decide whether the discounted price is actually worth it later.

Many credit cards provide benefits that can protect eligible purchases in case of accidental damage or theft. In some cases, you might also be able to receive reimbursement if a merchant won't accept an item for return. These perks could be especially useful if you plan on purchasing expensive holiday gifts, such as a new phone or television.

Here are some protection benefits to look out for when considering different types of credit cards (specific benefits can vary by card and card issuer):

Purchase protection: Covers eligible new purchases against damage or theft.

Extended warranty coverage: Provides additional warranty coverage to eligible purchases with existing manufacturer's warranties.

Cell phone protection: Covers eligible cell phones (on plans paid for by your applicable card) against damage or theft.

Return protection: Provides reimbursement for eligible new purchases if the retailer won't allow you to return them.

Check your card's benefits guide before you shop. These protections typically have coverage limits, exclusions, and other requirements.

Put your extra spending during the holidays to good use by earning a credit card welcome bonus on purchases you're already making.

Many credit cards require you to meet a spending threshold over the first few months to qualify for a sign-up bonus, so this could be a good time to align your increased spending with earning extra cash back, points, or miles.

Before you apply, make sure you can meet the spending requirement with purchases you've already budgeted for. Spending more than you planned just to earn a welcome bonus can cost you more than the bonus is worth.

It's common for credit card issuers like American Express, Chase, and Citi to provide targeted shopping offers to cardholders. These offers can help you save money if you make an eligible purchase from a specified retailer, and your targeted offers can vary.

For example, you might see an offer in your online account for 10% back on a Holiday Inn stay or 5% cash back on Sony electronics. These offers may not add a ton to your overall budget, but they can add up if you receive offers for purchases you were going to make anyway.

To use an offer, add it to your account, then make the eligible purchase with that credit card. There's often a limit on how much you can save, so be sure to read the offer details carefully.

articles.title: Prejuízo dos Correios atinge R$ 7,5 bilhões no terceiro trimestre | G1
articles.standfirst: Rombo da estatal aumentou em relação ao mesmo período do ano passado, quando registrou prejuízo de R$ 5,9 bilhões; empresa está em reestruturação
articles.summary: Prejuízo dos Correios chega a R$ 7,5 bilhões no 3º trimestre, o 16º déficit seguido da estatal que agora aposta em plano de reestruturação e novos empréstimos.
articles.body:
Ponto de Coleta dos Correios em Belém — Foto: Divulgação

Os Correios tiveram prejuízo de R$ 7,5 bilhões até o terceiro trimestre de 2026, segundo o balanço contábil da estatal. O resultado representa um crescimento do rombo registrado no segundo trimestre, quando a estatal já teve um prejuízo de R$ 5,6 bilhões.

Com isso, os Correios completam o 16º trimestre seguido com déficit nas contas . Na comparação com 2025, quando o rombo foi de R$ 5,9 bilhões, o prejuízo também aumentou. Apesar disso, a empresa afirma que o resultado veio R$ 272 milhões melhor do que o esperado.

"Os indicadores de receitas e despesas mostram que os resultados seguem em linha com o planejamento para 2026", diz a estatal em nota. Os Correios atualmente têm um plano de reestruturação para tentar recuperar suas contas.

Segundo a estatal, o prejuízo é resultado de "pressões relevantes" enfrentadas pelos Correios nos últimos anos. Entre elas, redução de receitas vindas dos serviços postais tradicionais, elevação dos custos operacionais e necessidade da estatal manter sua estrutura capilarizada, ou seja, presente em todo o país.

O demonstrativo financeiro mostra ainda que a receita total da empresa no terceiro trimestre chegou a R$ 13,2 bilhões. Já as despesas somaram R$ 20,7 bilhões, cerca de 1,2% abaixo do planejado.

A maior parte da receita dos Correios teve como origem serviços e vendas oferecidos pela empresa. Foram R$ 11,7 bilhões recebidos dessa forma. Ainda assim, houve queda de 5,33% na comparação com os resultados do mesmo período de 2025.

Com ações até 2027, o plano de reestruturação dos Correios busca reorganizar a empresa para diminuir custos e modernizar seu modelo de negócios. Segundo a estatal, os resultados dessas ações têm "diferentes prazos" e devem ser observados somente no futuro.

"O monitoramento do Plano de Reestruturação evidencia a evolução da implementação das iniciativas destinadas ao aumento da eficiência operacional, à recuperação da competitividade e ao fortalecimento da capacidade de geração de receitas", diz o relatório contábil.

Ainda segundo o documento, uma das prioridades dos Correios no momento é manter a liquidez da empresa enquanto o plano é colocado em prática. Para isso, em outubro deste ano — depois dos resultados do terceiro trimestre —, a estatal conseguiu a autorização formal para o empréstimo de R$ 7 bilhões, anunciado ainda nos resultados do segundo semestre .

O empréstimo conta com garantia do governo federal. Com sua concretização, os Correios chegaram a R$ 19 bilhões em empréstimos desde o fim de 2025. A nova quantia bilionária tinha previsão de entrar no caixa da estatal somente no início de novembro, segundo o relatório contábil.

"A contratação representa avanço relevante na execução da estratégia de financiamento da Empresa, contribuindo para o fortalecimento das perspectivas de liquidez e para a sustentação financeira das operações durante o período de implementação das medidas de reestruturação", diz o documento.

articles.title: Tata Steel eyes NINL merger this fiscal; Rs 40,000 crore expansion awaits clearance
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Tata Steel expects to bring Neelachal Ispat Nigam Ltd (NINL) under its fold through a merger within the current financial year, with the final
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Tata Steel expects to bring Neelachal Ispat Nigam Ltd (NINL) under its fold through a merger within the current financial year, with the final approval from the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) now awaited."The amalgamation of NINL with Tata Steel remains on track for completion this financial year," Koushik Chatterjee, Executive Director and Chief Financial Officer (CFO) of Tata Steel, said.The NCLT is scheduled to hear the matter later this month. Its final approval will pave the way for Tata Steel's proposed Rs 40,000 crore expansion at the NINL facility.Tata Steel acquired NINL's assets for Rs 12,100 crore through its erstwhile subsidiary, Tata Steel Long Products (TSLP). The acquisition was completed in July 2022 and included a steel manufacturing unit with an annual production capacity of 1 million tonnes per annum (MTPA).The company plans to add around 5 million tonnes of capacity to the facility, which is located about 5-10 km from its Kalinganagar steel plant. The proposed investment is part of Tata Steel's long products expansion plans in the region."We have... announced another 5 million tonne expansion in Neelachal (Ispat Nigam), which is also in Kalinganagar. It is a long products expansion, and we have announced that it is a Rs 40,000 crore project," Tata Steel CEO and Managing Director T V Narendran recently told PTI.NINL was the first state-owned steel company to be privatised by the Centre. Tata Steel is among the top global steelmakers, with an annual crude steel capacity of 36 million tonnes.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? articles.title: Megaspeed says Alice Huang exited company in 2025, stays silent on 'personal matters'
articles.summary: Singapore-based firm Megaspeed has confirmed that Alice Huang, the former executive at the centre of the controversy involving Nvidia's Jensen Huang, left
articles.body: Singapore-based firm Megaspeed has confirmed that Alice Huang, the former executive at the centre of the controversy involving Nvidia's Jensen Huang, left the company in August 2025.The company told CNBC on Sunday that Alice Huang officially departed on August 30, 2025, and no longer holds any role there. It declined to comment on her personal affairs.“Megaspeed does not comment on Ms. Huang’s personal and private matters,” the company said in an emailed statement.The announcement comes amid heightened scrutiny of Megaspeed following reports about Alice Huang's alleged relationship with Jensen Huang and her business connections in China. The New York Times has reported that US intelligence officials believe she was recruited by China's intelligence services to gather information on the Nvidia chief.Jensen Huang acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife amid the reports and resigned as Nvidia CEO on November 12. The reports also raised questions about another alleged relationship involving a senior Nvidia employee.Who is Alice Huang?Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, built a career in Chinese finance before moving into the artificial intelligence and cloud computing sector.She reportedly worked in television journalism before taking up roles in banking and investment management, including at HSBC's private banking arm in Hong Kong and Chinese investment bank CITIC Securities.She later held senior positions at Shanghai Hexi Investment Management, a Chinese investment firm, where she was identified in company records as a deputy general manager and executive director. She became the controlling shareholder of Megaspeed in March 2023, according to corporate records reviewed by research group C4ADS.Her business interests have also drawn attention because of reported links to Huawei. An investigation by private intelligence firm Tesari, shared with CNBC, found that Shanghai Hexi acquired a 27% stake in data centre developer Shanghai Century Longteng in 2021. Century Longteng held a controlling stake in Shenzhen Yifeng Technology, whose key customer was Huawei Cloud. Hexi exited its investment in Century Longteng in 2024.The findings establish an indirect business connection to infrastructure serving Huawei, but do not establish that the facility acquired Nvidia chips or that Alice Huang was involved in any unauthorised transfer of technology.Megaspeed under scrutiny over Nvidia chipsMegaspeed describes itself as a core regional business partner of Nvidia's cloud computing business. It allows customers to rent computing capacity powered by Nvidia graphics processing units (GPUs), specialised chips used for complex computing tasks.The company, which operates in Singapore and Indonesia, has previously faced media and government scrutiny over concerns that Nvidia chips supplied through its business may have been redirected to customers in China.Megaspeed rejected allegations concerning its business, supply chain and global operations, saying the media reports were not supported by verifiable evidence. It said it had appointed external legal counsel to conduct a thorough internal investigation.The company added that its operational and supply-chain controls were designed to comply with applicable laws, including US export control requirements and regulations in the markets where it operates.It said it would review the reports and communicate further with stakeholders as appropriate.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Sebi plans AI guardrails for capital markets, stresses human oversight in critical decisions
articles.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) will soon issue detailed guidelines for the responsible use of artificial intelligence (AI) in the
articles.body: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) will soon issue detailed guidelines for the responsible use of artificial intelligence (AI) in the capital markets, with a focus on investor protection, accountability and human oversight, chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said on Sunday.The proposed guidelines will lay down safeguards for AI applications used by market participants, including disclosure requirements and accountability of regulated entities. A 'human-in-the-loop' approach will also ensure that critical decisions involving AI remain subject to human oversight, Pandey said, according to PTI.The regulator had floated a consultation paper in June 2025 proposing guiding principles for the responsible use of AI and machine learning in the securities market. The proposed framework aims to harness the benefits of the technology while addressing risks to investor protection, market integrity and financial stability.Pandey was speaking at the inauguration of Sebi's pavilion, titled 'Bharat Ka Share Bazaar', at the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. The pavilion, inaugurated on November 14, has been set up in association with market institutions, including the National Stock Exchange (NSE), Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX), Central Depository Services (India) Ltd (CDSL), National Securities Depository Ltd (NSDL) and the Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI).The pavilion features an AI zone and an Investor Facilitation Camp, where visitors can interact with officials and learn about safe investment practices. It also aims to educate people about fraudulent investment schemes, unregistered entities and illegal mobilisation of funds.Pandey urged participating institutions to use their interactions with visitors to identify processes that could be simplified and services that could be improved. He also highlighted Sebi's 'Samajh Se Investing Simple' campaign under Project Jagrook and reiterated the message 'Check, Validate and Verify', asking investors to understand an investment, verify its authenticity and assess its risks before committing money.The regulator has also been strengthening its cybersecurity framework amid rising threats to financial institutions and cryptocurrency platforms, as well as digital frauds involving social media influencers. Sebi introduced a structured incident response mechanism in May, aligned with the Financial Stability Board's FIRE reporting template, Pandey said, reported ANI.On risks linked to quantum computing, the Sebi chief said the regulator was taking stock of cryptographic systems and identifying areas where the technology is used to assess potential vulnerabilities. Such risks could become more pronounced around 2032-35, making it important for markets to prepare in advance.Sebi has also developed supervisory tools, including 'Sudarshan', which is being showcased at international regulatory forums, and is working to strengthen its AI capabilities through global initiatives and supervisory toolkits.Sebi reviews listing framework for startupsPandey also said Sebi has set up a working group to examine ways to make the Innovators Growth Platform (IGP) more attractive to startups, particularly deep-tech and biotech firms that may take longer to become profitable.The existing platform has not gained the desired traction, and the regulator is considering changes that could help such companies access public markets at an earlier stage. The aim is to give investors a clearer understanding of the higher risks involved while allowing them to participate in the companies' long-term growth potential.The 45th IITF, organised by the India Trade Promotion Organisation, is being held at Bharat Mandapam from November 14 to 27. This year's theme is 'Vikas aur Virasat'.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.

articles.title: Manipal Hospitals Q2 revenue grows 37.3%; net profit rises 21.6%
articles.summary: Manipal Hospitals Q2 revenue rose 37.3% to Rs 3,399 crore; net profit ex-exceptionals up 21.6% to Rs 380 crore, with margins declining.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Manipal Health Enterprises, which operates Manipal Hospitals, reported a 37.3% year-on-year increase in revenue from operations to Rs 3,399 crore in the September quarter, compared with Rs 2,475 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.Net profit, excluding exceptional items, rose 21.6% to Rs 380 crore from Rs 313 crore. However, the net profit margin contracted by 140 basis points to 11.2% from 12.6% a year earlier. Reported net profit, including exceptional items, stood at Rs 285 crore, against Rs 318 crore in Q2 FY26.EBITDA increased 29.8% to Rs 882 crore, compared with Rs 680 crore in the year-ago quarter. EBITDA margin, however, declined to 26% from 27.5%, a contraction of 150 basis points. The company attributed its performance to sustained patient demand, growth in high-acuity specialties and improved capacity utilisation across its network.The current quarter’s results include Sahyadri Hospitals, which Manipal acquired in October last year, while the corresponding year-ago period does not include that acquisition. Sahyadri contributed Rs 375 crore in revenue and Rs 73 crore in EBITDA during the quarter.Commenting on the performance, Dilip Jose, managing director and CEO of Manipal Hospitals, said growth was driven by higher patient volumes, with more people accessing its healthcare services. Improved capacity utilisation, particularly in high-acuity specialties, was another key contributor.He said the company would continue to focus on strengthening clinical capabilities, improving operational performance and building a more integrated healthcare platform.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: SpaceX Catches Starship From Orbit for the First Time. Here’s What It Means for Starlink’s Costs
articles.summary: Key TakeawaysSpaceX caught a Starship upper stage returning from orbit for the first time on Nov. 14, though it lost the Super Heavy booster on the same flig...
articles.body:
SpaceX caught a Starship upper stage returning from orbit for the first time on Nov. 14, though it lost the Super Heavy booster on the same flight.

Starship spending is weighing on the Space segment, which posted a $7 million operating loss in the third quarter, against $259 million in operating income a year earlier.

Most of the payoff from reusable ships would go to Starlink. Connectivity earned $2.37 billion in operating income last quarter, and 75% of the mass SpaceX put in orbit was its own payloads.

The stock closed Friday at $139.11, about 3% above its $135 IPO price. A caught ship flying again quickly matters more to the stock than the first catch itself.

SpaceX ( SPCX:NASDAQ ) caught a Starship upper stage with its launch tower for the first time on Saturday, Nov. 14, about 22.5 hours after Flight 15 lifted off from Starbase. Ship 42 flew 14 orbits and deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites before the tower's arms closed around it, CNBC reported . "Mechazilla has caught the Starship," SpaceX's Dan Huot said on the company's livestream, Universe Today reported.

The flight wasn't clean. The Super Heavy booster's catch was called off minutes after liftoff on Friday, Nov. 13, when its onboard systems flagged a fuel-system problem, and it exploded before reaching the Gulf of Mexico. The catch also raises the bar for Rocket Lab ( RKLB:NASDAQ ), whose reusable Neutron rocket hasn't flown: Rocket Lab signed eight Neutron missions worth more than $515 million last quarter, but its first launch has slipped into 2027.

The case for the catch is cost. Starship carries far more than Falcon 9: Flight 14's 26 V3 satellites added about 10 times the downlink capacity of a Falcon 9 Starlink launch, according to SpaceX's third-quarter results . SpaceX is also its own biggest customer. Of the 476 metric tons it put in orbit in the third quarter, 358 tons, or 75%, were its own payloads, mostly Starlink satellites. A ship that comes back to the tower instead of burning up is what turns that capacity into cheaper launches.

Starship Spending Weighs on SpaceX's Space Segment

Right now, Starship is a cost. SpaceX's revenue reached $14.58 billion in the third quarter, almost double the second quarter's $7.81 billion, but the Space segment contributed little of that growth.

The Space segment brought in $1.77 billion and lost $7 million, against a $259 million profit a year earlier. SpaceX said faster Starship R&D drove a $367 million rise in the segment's costs, and it spent $1.61 billion on Space capex, about 91% of the segment's revenue. Starlink is where the payoff should land: Connectivity earned $2.37 billion in operating income on $5.25 billion of revenue, a 45% margin, before any savings from reusable ships.

articles.title: Indian Railways has built freight corridors, but can it win back cargo from road transport & highways?
articles.summary: By Jagannarayan Padmanabhan Indian Railways is entering a new phase in freight transportation.
articles.body: By Jagannarayan PadmanabhanIndian Railways is entering a new phase in freight transportation.The eastern and western dedicated freight corridors (DFCs) are now fully operational, unlocking capacity and enabling faster, more reliable freight movement. More capacity is on the horizon, with a proposed east-west corridor set to strengthen connectivity across the country.After decades of investment constraints, rail freight finally has the infrastructure to compete. But infrastructure alone will not win back traffic from roads.The challenge is no longer building tracks. It is persuading customers to choose rail over trucks.At first glance, rail freight appears to be thriving. Freight loading has risen from 1,098 million tonne in fiscal 2015 to 1,617 million tonne in fiscal 2025 and a record 1,670 million tonne last fiscal. Yet rail's position within India's logistics system remains weaker than these numbers imply.A parliamentary committee recently estimated rail's share of national freight tonnage at only about 27% in fiscal 2025, well below the National Rail Plan's goal of 45% by 2030.The issue is not a shortage of freight. India's economy generates more than enough cargo to support that ambition. The problem is that roads are increasingly serving customers better.The competitive pressure is visible even in commodities that have traditionally been rail strongholds. Coal, iron ore, steel and cement remain the backbone of railway freight earnings, with coal alone contributing nearly half of freight revenue. Yet roads have steadily expanded their presence across several of these segments.Coal offers the clearest example. Road's share of raw-coal dispatches increased from 24.4% in fiscal 2021 to 33.8% in fiscal 2024 before easing slightly to 31.1% in fiscal 2025.Over the same period, rail's share fell from 53.9% to 47.4% before recovering to 50.5%. Rail may have regained some ground, but roads are now firmly established even in one of its most important freight categories.A similar story emerges elsewhere. Railways moved about 178 million tonne of iron ore in fiscal 2025 against production of roughly 289 million tonne, implying a rail transportation coefficient of just over 60%. Comparable ratios were materially lower for steel and cement. While these figures do not directly measure modal share, they underscore a broader point: a substantial portion of India's bulk freight still moves outside the rail network.The reasons extend far beyond pricing.India's freight geography is changing. Urbanisation, rising incomes and e-commerce are shifting consumption away from a handful of metropolitan centres towards hundreds of Tier II and III cities. India's urban population is estimated to have reached 522 million in 2025 and is projected to approach 600 million by 2036.More revealing is where demand growth is occurring. Tier II and III cities are estimated to have generated around two-thirds of incremental direct-to-consumer orders last fiscal. Warehousing, distribution and industrial activity are following the same trajectory, creating a logistics network that is increasingly dispersed.Road transport has adapted quickly to this reality. Supported by a national highway network that has expanded nearly 60%, from 91,287 km in 2014 to 146,204 km by March 2025, trucks can reach new warehouses, distributors, factories and construction sites directly. They offer flexibility, minimal handling and a single point of accountability from origin to destination.Rail, by contrast, remains primarily a line-haul business.Its challenge is not its dependence on trucks for first-mile and last-mile connectivity. Every major freight system relies on multimodal logistics. The problem is that the transition between rail and road often remains fragmented, creating additional handling, delays and uncertainty for customers.A cement producer or steel manufacturer does not evaluate only the railway tariff. It evaluates the cost, speed and reliability of the entire journey. A lower rail rate becomes irrelevant if cargo must be handled multiple times, delivery windows are uncertain or information is unavailable. Customers buy logistics outcomes, not transport modes.That is why the next frontier for Indian Railways is service quality.The DFCs will improve transit times, but faster line-haul movement is only part of the solution. Customers also need assured wagon availability, predictable departures, reliable arrival schedules and real-time shipment visibility. A steel plant cannot afford disruptions in raw-material supplies because wagons are delayed. An exporter cannot risk missing a vessel because cargo reaches the port late.Railways should therefore measure success not only through loading volumes and freight revenue but also through customer-centric metrics such as on-time arrivals, terminal turnaround times, schedule adherence and customer retention.Reliability must become a product.The same customer-first approach should guide the next phase of cargo-terminal development.The Gati Shakti Cargo Terminal programme has already expanded freight-handling capacity. The next step is to transform these facilities into integrated logistics hubs where cargo can be consolidated, stored, containerised and transferred seamlessly between rail and road.Success will depend less on the number of terminals built and more on where they are located and how effectively they connect with surrounding logistics networks. Facilities should emerge where manufacturing, warehousing and consumption are growing, not simply where railway land is available.Partnerships will be equally important. Railways need not extend tracks to every customer. Instead, it should work more closely with trucking companies, warehouse operators and third-party logistics providers to create integrated door-to-door solutions. Digital platforms offering unified booking, tracking and shipment visibility across modes can further simplify the customer experience.The objective should be simple: make using rail as easy as using a truck.A manufacturer does not necessarily need a private siding, a full rake or even the lowest freight rate. It needs dependable delivery at a predictable total logistics cost. In many cases, the winning solution will not be rail versus road, but rail and road working together.India has largely solved the capacity problem in freight rail. The bigger challenge now is commercial. Roads have gained market share because they have aligned themselves more closely with customers' needs and adapted faster to the country's evolving freight geography.The future of freight will not be decided by who can move the most cargo, but who can serve the customer best.Indian Railways has built the infrastructure, now it must build the service model. Only then can it convert freight capacity into freight market share.(The author is Senior Director and Group Head, Consulting, Crisil Intelligence)Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: India, Egypt to explore possible trade pact with focus on farmers, fishermen and small workers
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India and Egypt will explore the possibility of a trade agreement to boost bilateral trade and investment while safeguarding the interests of
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India and Egypt will explore the possibility of a trade agreement to boost bilateral trade and investment while safeguarding the interests of farmers, fishermen and small workers in both countries, Union commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal said on Sunday.Speaking in Cairo, Goyal said officials from the two countries would first prepare the terms of reference to define the scope of a possible agreement and identify areas of mutual benefit."Once the terms of reference are set, we'll find out what we can realistically achieve and how much a boost we can get in both investment and trade," Goyal told ANI."We'll also figure out how to do all this without harming each other's farmers or fishermen," he added.He said the discussions would also take into account the impact on small workers and explore areas where the two economies could complement each other.Addressing the India-Egypt Business Forum earlier in the day, Goyal said the two sides would consider whether a preferential trade agreement or a free trade agreement would be more suitable.Goyal expressed confidence that India and Egypt would achieve the bilateral trade target of $12 billion set by the leaders of the two countries. He said both sides were looking to expand trade further."We will definitely meet that bilateral trade target between the two countries. Beyond that, we want to make a bigger leap," he said.Bilateral trade in goods rose 64% year-on-year to $5.04 billion during April-September 2026, according to a commerce ministry release dated November 14.In the 2025-26 financial year, India's goods exports to Egypt stood at $3.87 billion, while imports from the country were valued at $2.60 billion. This took total bilateral goods trade to $6.47 billion.Goyal arrived in Cairo on November 14 for a two-day official visit on November 15 and 16, accompanied by a delegation of more than 130 business leaders and startup representatives, the Commerce Ministry said.During the visit, he co-chaired the seventh India-Egypt Joint Trade Committee meeting with Egypt's Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade, Mohamed Farid Saleh.The programme also includes a Joint Business Council meeting and the Egypt-India Startups Forum.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Urban Company shareholders approve Rs 2,500 cr raise
articles.summary: Urban Company shareholders approve raising up to Rs 2,500 crore to fund InstaHelp expansion and acquisitions, even as Sept-quarter loss widens to Rs 182.5 crore.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Urban Company’s shareholders have approved a proposal to raise up to Rs 2,500 crore, as the home services platform spends on expanding its instant house-help business InstaHelp.In its October shareholders’ letter, Urban Company said the proposed capital would give it flexibility to invest across its businesses, strengthen InstaHelp’s position and pursue potential acquisitions. It held Rs 1,901 crore in cash and treasury investments at the end of September.The approval comes after Urban Company reported a net loss of Rs 182.5 crore for the September quarter, more than triple the Rs 59.3 crore loss a year earlier. Total income rose 40% to Rs 578.5 crore. InstaHelp’s orders grew 63% from the preceding quarter to about 62 lakh. Its net order value fell to Rs 114 from Rs 138, which the company attributed to competition and introductory pricing for new users.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? articles.title: India’s semiconductor industry boom may add over 1 lakh jobs in India in 3 years, with 67,500 openings in 18 months; senior engineers command up to 6 times IT services salaries
articles.summary: India is betting big on the semiconductor industry to drive an important phase of its manufacturing leap and the focus is expected to create over one lakh
articles.body: India is betting big on the semiconductor industry to drive an important phase of its manufacturing leap and the focus is expected to create over one lakh jobs in the coming years.Industry experts estimate over 1 lakh jobs in the next three years through the country’s efforts to build a semiconductor ecosystem of its own.Hiring requirements in the semiconductor industry are also evolving, with recruitment extending beyond conventional chip-design roles.Talent hunt in semiconductor industryAccording to estimates by Boston Consulting Group (BCG), the country’s semiconductor workforce, currently pegged at 25,000, is expected to expand fourfold during this period.Separately, a study by recruitment and staffing firm CIEL HR Services for ET indicates that companies in the sector could add around 67,500 jobs in the next 18 months.Professionals with specialised skills, including process engineering, chip fabrication, chip design, systems engineering and product architecture, can earn four to six times the salaries of IT services professionals with similar experience. The difference is particularly pronounced at the mid-to-senior levels, Ankush Wadhera, partner and managing director at BCG told the financial daily.“The supply of fit-for-role talent is not keeping pace with demand and, as a result, many players are looking outside India for senior talent,” said Wadhera.The US and Southeast Asia have emerged as key destinations for companies seeking experienced professionals, with a significant share of the global talent pool comprising members of the Indian diaspora.“Entry-level and mid-level talent can be easily trained, but it is senior talent that is in acute shortage in the country,” he said.Specialists in focusCompanies are increasingly looking for specialists in process engineering, equipment maintenance, yield management, reliability engineering and advanced packaging, areas that involve high-value technical work.A CIEL HR Services study estimates that India has around 1.5 lakh semiconductor professionals working across chip design, verification, engineering, testing and product development.“About 43% of the workforce has more than 10 years of experience, while nearly three-fourths have over five years of experience,” said Aditya Narayan Mishra, CEO of CIEL HR Services.A study of India’s semiconductor industry, found that Qualcomm has the highest number of current job openings in the sector. AMD ranks second, followed by Nvidia, Synopsys, Applied Materials, Infineon, Cadence and Micron.“For years, India’s semiconductor workforce was almost entirely focused on design,” said Mishra. “Domestic fabrication and packaging units are now creating demand for roles in process engineering, equipment maintenance, yield management, reliability and advanced packaging, which until recently accounted for a negligible share of hiring.”The shortage of skilled professionals remains acute. The study found that for every 100 engineers with expertise in microarchitecture, the semiconductor industry has 135 vacancies to fill.Companies are looking beyond competitors in the semiconductor industry to meet their hiring requirements, increasingly tapping academic institutions and IT services firms for talent. Among the skills in greatest demand are physical design and timing closure, digital design and RTL (register transfer level) coding, and design verification.Employers are also seeking professionals skilled in microarchitecture, emulation, formal verification, embedded systems and silicon bring-up. Proficiency in programming languages such as Python, C++, Verilog and SystemVerilog, which is used for hardware description and verification, is another sought-after skill.For its analysis, CIEL examined semiconductor recruitment trends in India over the 12 months leading up to November 2026. The study covered approximately 45,000 job openings across more than 150 semiconductor companies.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.

articles.title: Oister Global launches Rs 600 cr deeptech fund
articles.summary: Oister Global launches Sebi-registered Rs 400 crore deeptech fund with Rs 200 crore greenshoe to back 8-10 Indian growth-stage tech firms.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Investment firm Oister Global has launched a growth-stage deeptech fund targeting Rs 400 crore, with an option to raise an additional Rs 200 crore, as it looks to back Indian technology companies ready to scale up operations.The Oister Deep Tech Fund, registered as a Sebi Category II alternative investment fund, will invest in 8-10 companies across space technology, defence and aerospace, semiconductors, quantum technologies, advanced mobility, advanced materials and energy storage. It will have a six-year tenure, extendable by two years with investor approval.The fund will target companies with proven technologies, proprietary intellectual property, paying customers and multiple revenue streams. The capital will be used to expand production, fulfil orders and support commercial expansion. Oister said it had shortlisted a few potential investments but did not disclose their names.“Deep tech founders in India run a different race from software startups. They spend years building a product, then need serious capital to manufacture and sell it, and most growth investors are not set up to wait that long,” said Sandeep Sinha, co-founder and co-CEO of Oister Global.Co-founder and co-CEO Rohit Bhayana said relatively few funds support companies at the stage when technology must be turned into a scalable business.The launch comes amid growing investment in Indian deeptech. Startups in the sector raised nearly $3 billion across 189 deals in 2025, according to data cited by Oister. However, only 18 of the 453 Indian deep-science startups and spinouts tracked by WIPO had reached late-stage funding.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? articles.title: WPI inflation, FII flows, crude oil prices to guide markets this week
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Domestic inflation data, foreign investor activity, crude oil prices and developments in West Asia are expected to influence stock market
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Domestic inflation data, foreign investor activity, crude oil prices and developments in West Asia are expected to influence stock market sentiment this week.Globally, investors will track US retail sales, Nvidia's earnings and minutes of the Federal Reserve's latest policy meeting for cues on economic growth, interest rates and technology stocks.October wholesale price index (WPI) inflation and merchandise trade data, both scheduled for release on Monday, November 16, will also be among the key domestic indicators."Movements in crude oil, the dollar, US Treasury yields and FII flows will remain important determinants of market direction. The domestic economic calendar will be busy, with October WPI inflation and merchandise trade data scheduled for Monday, 16 November," Ajit Mishra, SVP - Research at Religare Broking, told PTI.Globally, investors will also monitor US jobless claims and the minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting for signals on the US economy and the likely direction of monetary policy, he added.Siddhartha Khemka, Head of Research, Wealth Management, at Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd, said Indian equities could extend their recent gains."Indian equities are expected to trade with a positive bias this week, extending their gradual upmove. Record buying by foreign institutional investors, strong domestic fundamentals and encouraging second-quarter earnings season support the positive sentiment."Globally, investors will track Japan's GDP, US retail sales, UK and EU inflation, US jobs data and the Federal Reserve's meeting minutes," he said.Foreign investors made a strong return to Indian equities in the first half of November, investing Rs 84,290 crore after two consecutive months of net outflows. The inflows came amid a global sell-off in AI-related stocks, lower crude oil prices and attractive valuations of large-cap shares.Developments in global markets, particularly volatility in technology stocks, will also influence domestic sentiment, analysts said.Ponmudi R, CEO of online trading and wealth technology firm Enrich Money, said concerns over high artificial intelligence valuations and the sustainability of semiconductor investments had triggered intermittent selling in global technology stocks."A deeper correction in this segment could dampen broader risk appetite and weigh on sentiment towards Indian IT companies. Investors will also monitor US Treasury yields and the dollar, as further strength in either could tighten financial conditions and influence capital flows into emerging markets," he said.Crude oil prices and currency movements will remain other important external factors, he added.Hariselvan Radhakrishnan, founder and CEO of research analyst firm HST Wealth, said developments in the US bond market would be important for foreign investment flows."Strong US retail activity or hawkish signals in the Federal Open Market Committee minutes could reinforce expectations of tighter monetary conditions, keeping Treasury yields above the 5 per cent threshold. Crude oil presents another important variable for domestic sentiment," he said.Indian benchmark indices ended higher last week. The 30-share BSE Sensex gained 564.43 points, or 0.69%, while the 50-share NSE Nifty rose 113.95 points, or 0.45%.(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India.)Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.

articles.title: Cab secy assures homebuyers on their proposals for stronger RERA safeguards
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Amid focus on rollout of next generation of reforms for ease of living across sectors (Deregulation 3.0), including in real estate, cabinet
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Amid focus on rollout of next generation of reforms for ease of living across sectors (Deregulation 3.0), including in real estate, cabinet secretary TV Somanathan has assured a national homebuyers’ body that their suggestions for strengthening legal provisions to protect buyers’ interests would be looked into.The suggestions of the homebuyers’ body include a statutory exit option enabling buyers to secure hassle-free refunds upon cancellation and direct, automatic compensation payouts for project delays to all allottees without requiring individual, time-consuming legal complaints.To protect buyers’ interests, the Forum for People’s Collective Efforts (FPCE) had written to PM Narendra Modi seeking separation of promotion of the real estate sector from regulation in place of a common entity (RERA) carrying out both tasks and had sent a copy to Somanathan. Responding to it, the cabinet secretary replied that the “thoughtful, well-analysed and wide-ranging suggestions” will be taken into consideration.FPCE president Abhay Upadhyay said that following this, they met senior officials in the Cabinet Secretariat and held a detailed discussion, submitting more suggestions. They have suggested provision of a “binding statutory Agreement for Sale” by including it as a schedule to the RERA law. “Builders continue to insert clauses that defeat the Act, and the agreements carrying them are uploaded on the RERA authorities’ websites without scrutiny,” FPCE said.The organisation also suggested setting up of a National Appellate Tribunal for Real Estate, replacing poorly constituted state tribunals, with statutory appeals heard directly by the Supreme Court-based central forum utilising virtual benches to ensure uniform RERA enforcement nationwide and further appeals lying with the Supreme Court. “National tribunal should hear appeals against orders of RERAs and of the adjudicating officers alike; it should sit through virtual benches scaled to caseload so that no homebuyer need travel to Delhi,” it said.Proposing the statutory exit option for buyers, FPCE said that Section 18 of RERA addresses developer’s default and nothing else. A buyer who opts to withdraw for reasons of their own — loss of employment, death of an earning member — has no exit option and forfeits whatever money the builder chooses to withhold. It suggested hassle-free refunds upon cancellation — 100% within one year of booking and a full refund plus SBI savings-rate interest thereafter — preventing builders from withholding up to 75% of buyer payments in such cases.It also suggested periodic audits and independent order scrutiny of RERAs to curb lax, pro-promoter enforcement, alongside placing a non-negotiable Agreement for Sale in a statutory schedule. FPCE has suggested mandatory direct payouts to all allottees via a simple one-page claim through the authority, eliminating prolonged individual legal battles.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Haven't saved enough for retirement? Wealthy people haven't either.
articles.summary: Wealthy Americans say they will need $2.6 million to feel financially set to retire, according to a new study.
articles.body:
The rich aren't that different from you and me.

They also agonize about having enough money set aside for retirement — even if the amount they need to "retire comfortably" is loftier.

Wealthy Americans say they will need $2.6 million to feel financially set to retire, up 26% from last year, according to a new study from financial services firm HSBC.

That savings target is roughly double the amount that less-wealthy workers aim for.

"For affluent households, it's not simply about accumulating a larger nest egg, but ensuring their wealth can sustain their desired lifestyle over several decades," Jessie Zhu, an HSBC managing director, told Yahoo Finance.

The problem is, wealthy savers are only halfway toward reaching their goal on average. Baby boomers, those nearest to retirement, have hit 74% of their target, while millennials clock in at just 42%.

That trend holds for those lower on the economic ladder, other surveys have found.

About half of workers surveyed by Schroders have less than $500,000 in savings at retirement — including 24% who say it's unlikely they will have $250,000 set aside.

Northwestern Mutual found that nearly half of workers it surveyed don't expect to be financially prepared and believe there's a good chance they'll outlive their savings.

To help fill the coffers, nearly two-thirds of affluent Americans plan to stretch out their earnings years by slowly trimming back their working hours over time, the HSBC data found.

But formal phased retirement programs that offer a reduced or flexible schedule and a lighter workload have been few and far between. Last year, just 7% of firms surveyed by the Society for Human Resource Management (SHRM) offered a formal program. A larger share—about 2 in 10— offered an informal arrangement in which workers create their own plan with their manager.

Like wealthier Americans, working longer is the fallback position for most of us. More than 4 in 10 workers expect to work past age 65 or do not plan to retire, according to Transamerica research.

But the harsh reality is that most people retire before they reach 65 due to a health issue, caregiving for an aging relative, or a job loss.

So how much should you be saving? It depends on many variables, including where you live, how expensive your lifestyle is, your health, and your financial obligations.

In general, you should aim to have 10 times your pre-retirement income saved by the time you reach age 67. If you have an annual salary of $100,000, that means $1 million saved by the time you retire.

Kerry Hannon is a Senior Columnist at Yahoo Finance. She is a career and retirement strategist and the author of 14 books, including " Retirement Bites: A Gen X Guide to Securing Your Financial Future, " " In Control at 50+: How to Succeed in the New World of Work ," and "Never Too Old to Get Rich.

articles.title: Jensen Huang discusses comeback as Nvidia CEO with allies, FT reports
articles.summary: Nov 15 () - Jensen Huang is considering a comeback as Nvidia's chief executive, and ‌has discussed with confidants the possibility of ‌returning, the Financi...
articles.body:
Nov 15 (Reuters) - Jensen Huang is considering a comeback as Nvidia's chief executive, and ‌has discussed with confidants the possibility of ‌returning, the Financial Times reported on Sunday, citing people ​familiar with the matter.

One Huang ally told the FT they were putting together a "war room" of Silicon Valley executives to lobby for the former ‌Nvidia chief's return ⁠and would try to garner support from the White House.

"Everyone that matters in ⁠tech outside the frontier labs loves Jensen," the person said, adding that the efforts had ​Huang's support.

The ​report comes days after ​the FT reported ‌that Nvidia's board had approached British chipmaker Arm Holdings CEO Rene Haas in its search for a potential successor to Jensen Huang.

Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment outside ‌regular business hours.

Huang stepped ​down on Thursday after revelations ​of extramarital affairs, ​including one involving a suspected Chinese ‌spy that raised questions ​over exports of ​the company's advanced AI chips to China. The scandal has plunged the chipmaker into ​crisis and ‌sent shockwaves across an AI industry he ​helped bankroll.

(Reporting by Disha Mishra in Bengaluru; ​Editing by Andrea Ricci)

articles.title: 'Everyone influential in tech loves Jenson': Huang discusses comeback as Nvidia CEO with allies - report
articles.summary: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is discussing a return to the company just days after stepping down following revelations of an affair with Alice Huang, a
articles.body: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is discussing a return to the company just days after stepping down following revelations of an affair with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman suspected by US authorities of spying for Beijing, and a separate alleged relationship with a subordinate, the Financial Times reported.According to one of Huang’s allies, the former CEO is assembling a task force of technology executives to push for his reinstatement. His supporters also plan to seek backing from the White House, with Huang reportedly supporting their efforts.Also Read | Trump backed Nvidia's Jensen Huang till end, urged him to fight for job amid China spy scandal: ReportHuang was succeeded by Nvidia CFO Colette Kress, who has taken over as interim CEO.“Everyone influential in tech, except the leading labs developing the most advanced AI models, loves Jensen,” the Huang ally told FT.A public campaign for his return gathered momentum over the weekend. An open letter urging Nvidia’s board to “Bring Jensen Back” was endorsed by several prominent figures, including Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney.Also Read | Nvidia employees want Jensen Huang back as CEO; internal suggestion box post draws over 1,600 commentHuang also retains support among some Nvidia employees, several of whom publicly called for his reinstatement and signed an open letter following his departure.Major investors have also appealed to the board. In a letter published on November 13, Altimeter Capital founder Brad Gerstner and Atreides Management head Gavin Baker urged directors to consider all options, including Huang’s possible return. They pointed to Nvidia’s years of success under his leadership and the uncertainty surrounding the company following his departure.However, even among those campaigning for Huang’s return, there are concerns about the challenges involved in restoring his reputation. One participant acknowledged to that an alleged affair with a subordinate could constitute grounds for dismissal.Additionally, the campaign could face resistance from influential US officials. On November 15, US treasury secretary Scott Bessent called for a “radical overhaul” of Nvidia’s leadership following Huang’s departure.Also Read | 'They need dramatic shakeup': Trump aide Bessent urges Nvidia to look outside company for new CEOUnlike some other technology founders, Huang did not hold a controlling stake that would have allowed him to overturn the board’s decision.Nvidia announced Huang’s departure on November 12 and appointed Kress as interim CEO. The company is scheduled to publish its quarterly results on Tuesday.Reports concerning Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang have also raised questions about Nvidia’s compliance with regulations governing AI chip sales to Asian customers with potential links to China.Meanwhile, Nvidia’s board is considering other potential candidates. The FT reported on November 13 that directors had approached Arm CEO Rene Haas as a possible successor. However, the board told the publication that it had not yet begun a “formal” selection process.Representatives for Nvidia and Huang declined to comment on the possibility of his return.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: 75% of hit-and-run victims miss out on compensation: Report
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Around 75% of eligible hit-and-run victims and their families miss out on compensation provided in the Motor Vehicles Act, according to a new
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Around 75% of eligible hit-and-run victims and their families miss out on compensation provided in the Motor Vehicles Act, according to a new report based on govt data on hit-and-run cases and compensations disbursed.The report by Primus Partners, a management consultancy firm, revealed that close to 70,000 hit-and-run cases are reported annually on average, claiming over 30,000 lives and leaving another 16,000 people seriously injured. Going by the compensation norm in the MV Act, the total annual compensation, taking into account all cases, should be around Rs 600 crore. However, less than Rs 300 crore has been disbursed in four years, highlighting a stark delivery gap.The updated Compensation to Victims of Hit and Run Motor Accidents Scheme rolled out in Feb 2022 provides Rs 2 lakh for death and Rs 50,000 for grievous injury.The report said, "As against an annual average 30,000 deaths and 16,000 grievous hurt victims due to hit-and-run accidents, number of claims registered have been less than 10,000 annually. Further, even after registering claims, less than 8,000 claimants have received compensation annually. As a result, less than 25% of Centre's yearly obligation of more than Rs 600 cr was disbursed, even four years after scheme's implementation."The report listed the hurdles, including low awareness and information asymmetry, complex and lengthy process, administrative bottlenecks, redundant disbursal layers and deterrent undertakings. It found that more than 80% of the respondents were completely unaware of the scheme, and 84% of those who knew about it did not know where to find forms or guidelines.It recommended the scheme's implementation through the district police department so that the compensation procedure is initiated suo motu immediately after a road crash is classified as hit and run. To transition to a digital, system-initiated process, it recommended migrating the scheme's implementation to the eDAR platform."Integrating the network of Common Service Centres into the scheme framework could help victims in submitting basic details on eDAR... Apart from transforming the scheme implementation framework, it is also critical to ensure a formula-based annual revision of compensation amount, for which budgetary support or other sources of funds may need to be tapped by the Union govt of India," the report said.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Trump, McDonald’s and Burger King among targets of past X posts that contain redirected website links
articles.summary: Some website links included in the X posts of politicians, government agencies and companies were redirected this weekend with unrelated videos, images and websites.
articles.body: Some website links included in the X posts of politicians, government agencies and companies were redirected this weekend to unrelated videos, images and websites. Links dating as far back as 2009 from URL-shortening service Bitly were affected, and only corporate and political X accounts appear to have been targeted, with President Donald Trump’s personal account seemingly hit the hardest. At least a dozen of Trump’s posts on X now direct to various inappropriate and unrelated sites. Public figures — like Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates, former Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau and former Vice President Mike Pence — as well as fast-food chains McDonald’s and Burger King, were also hit to varying degrees. Bitly URLs are shortened while holding the original and longer link. Bitly links do not automatically expire, according to the company’s website, but paid users can redirect links. Bitly said Sunday afternoon in a post on X that it had “identified an issue that allowed bad actors to repurpose certain old, inactive links to redirect people to content unrelated to the original posts.” The company said it suspended the accounts that altered links and were working to disable the affected URLs. “Our Trust and Safety team is working to address the issue and strengthen protections against similar misuse in the future,” Bitly wrote. Both Bitly and X have not yet responded to CNN’s request for comment. It’s unclear whether hackers made custom Bitly links, which effectively allow them to copy the original URL and redirect to any website. That may have been possible if the original Bitly link to the website no longer exists or has expired. Bitly links may be susceptible to artificial intelligence scans and exploiting mechanisms to redirect links, noted Ari Lightman, a digital media professor at Carnegie Mellon University’s Heinz College of Information Systems and Public Policy. The redirected links seem confined to posts made between 2009 and 2014. Lightman said that some social media accounts are not monitored, “and that’s problematic.” Changing unmonitored links could expose user information when clicking those links, he warned, highlighting the importance of internet safety. “You have a variety of vulnerabilities that people can utilize for exploitation,” said Lightman. “It’s just finding these old messages out there and sort of repopulating them,” often for malicious purposes. A 2013 post from Trump criticizing wind turbines that used a Bitly link now redirects to a Google site titled “fortnite baby” and includes a photo of a baby. Another 2013 post from Trump tagged former Republican nominee for president Mitt Romney, and links to the popular game “Geometry Dash.” One of Trump’s posts about his golf course in Scotland includes a link to an Epstein files Wikipedia page. “It sounds like they’re trying to make some sort of a message tying these sites into Donald Trump’s policies, and sometimes it’s just vulgar mechanisms,” said Lightman. Public officials and company heads who often circulated Bitly links were also targeted. A post in 2010 from Microsoft founder Bill Gates contains the text, “Notes from D.C. trip. Spoke w/former President Clinton at the Foreign Relations committee aid programs are working,” and includes a Bitly link of a Reddit page that has an animated image from a fabricated posting by former New York City Mayor Michael Bloomberg. A post in 2011 by Trudeau contains a Bitly link that redirects to a vulgar YouTube audio clip. A 2011 post from Burger King intended to provide restaurant locations was redirected to a Wikipedia page on a list of Nazi concentration camps, while another post linked to a Wikipedia page on Adolf Hitler. McDonald’s account has a post from 2011 that redirected to a page about the September 11 attacks, while its Indonesia account made a 2013 post about a jingle that now links to an unrelated “Would you rather?” YouTube video. A spokesperson for Burger King told CNN the company has “no part in the links being redirected” and that it was “working quickly to correct and delete posts that have been altered.” McDonald’s did not immediately respond to CNN’s request for comment. Government accounts have also been ironically affected. A 2012 post from the FBI about computers infected by “Ghost Clicks” now directs to a page with a photo of a seal, while the Department of Defense account had a separately redirected post. A post by Pence seemingly directed to the same website as the FBI, despite being about an unrelated topic. Hijacking these links is especially concerning in the age of AI, says Lightman, because it allows manipulations to be made “en masse.”
